content.title: The Companion Whose Sincere Repentance Was Answered by Revelation
content.subtitle: A Heart Purified by Remorse and Embraced by Divine Forgiveness
content.body:
The incident took place in Madinatul Munawwarah. The Ansari Companion Ka‘b ibn ‘Amr, known as Abu Yusr (RA), openly narrated this mistake himself. A woman came to his shop to buy dates. Succumbing to a momentary whispering of Shaytan, he told her, “The dates inside the house are of better quality than these.” As soon as the woman entered the house, Abu Yusr (RA) lost control of himself, embraced her, and kissed her. The woman immediately became angry and frightened and said, “O servant of Allah! Fear Allah!”

A Confession Born of Inner Agony

Those words struck Abu Yusr (RA) like a thunderbolt. Trembling with intense fear and shame, he came out of the house. He first rushed to Abu Bakr (RA), confessed his sin, and asked, “Is there any repentance for my sin?” Abu Bakr (RA) said, “Keep the matter private and repent to Allah.” But the fire inside Abu Yusr’s heart did not subside. He then went to Umar (RA), who gave him the same advice. Finally, unable to bear the intense guilt within his heart, he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The Prophet ﷺ Remained Silent

Sitting before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and weeping, he said, “O Messenger of Allah! I touched a non-mahram woman, embraced her, and kissed her. But I did not commit adultery or engage in the ultimate forbidden act. I have come before you; give me whatever judgment Allah has decreed for me.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, deeply saddened, said, “You behaved in such a way with the family of a Mujahid who is absent in the path of Allah?” These calm yet weighty words of the Prophet ﷺ struck Abu Yusr’s heart like a burning arrow. Abu Yusr later narrated that at that moment he felt, “Alas! If only I had remained a disbeliever and had never accepted Islam until today, then at least I would not have had to face such a disgraceful sin before the Messenger of my Lord as a Muslim!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made no further comment and remained silent, as though the earth itself had become still, awaiting a final decree from the heavens.

The Consolation of Surah Hud and the Eternal Declaration of Forgiveness

A short while later, it was time for the Asr prayer. Abu Yusr (RA) offered the prayer behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with an extremely humble and remorseful heart. As soon as the prayer ended, Jibril (AS) descended with revelation. Allah revealed verse 114 of Surah Hud:

“And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Surely good deeds erase bad deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember.”

The Prophet ﷺ called Abu Yusr and recited this verse to him, saying, “Allah has forgiven this sin of yours.” Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) then stood up and asked, “O Messenger of Allah! Is this forgiveness specifically for Abu Yusr, or is it for all of us?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ clearly reassured them, saying, “No, rather, it is general for everyone among my Ummah.” (Source: Sahih al-Bukhari: 6823; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3124)

The Unfailing Power of Istighfar and Remorse

As human beings, we become entangled in hundreds of mistakes every day, knowingly or unknowingly. Yet, amid our busy lives and the deception of Shaytan, we often fail to find even a moment to seek forgiveness from our Lord. It is to break this spiritual stagnation and make Istighfar an inseparable part of our lives that Muslims Day has arranged this special journey of spiritual purification—The 10 Million Istighfar Challenge in 10 Days.
